description: Hand-written expectations for the ThreadDemo scenarios. Source lines come from the @GT markers in src/.

scenarios.title: Variable deleted by another thread (diagram scenario: main-owned var shared by T1 and T2)
scenarios.expected_conclusion: CResourceOwner::q3 (thread T2) deletes var and sets it to nullptr while CWorkerService::q2 (thread T1, via q1) still uses it. var is created in CScenarioRunner::runS1 and passed by std::ref to both threads. No lock or ownership rule protects it. q2 is only the failure site.
wrong_conclusions: the string 'Unknown exception' is the bad value

scenarios.title: Field value changed by another thread (singleton member, std::async writer, lambda reader)
scenarios.expected_conclusion: CReconfigService::applyProfile writes CSettings::m_mode (negative value) on an async thread while CCommandHandler::execute reads it on another thread; no lock. The 5 repeated errors per run form ONE cluster after normalization.

scenarios.title: Partial locking: writer locks, reader (native OS thread) does not
scenarios.expected_conclusion: CLedgerWriter::post updates m_debit and m_credit in two steps under CAccountLedger::m_mutex, but CLedgerAuditor::audit reads both without taking the mutex, so it can see debit != credit. A lock exists but only on one side.
wrong_conclusions: there is no lock in the code
the writer is missing a lock

scenarios.title: Control: both sides lock the same mutex, error is an ordering problem, NOT a data race
scenarios.expected_conclusion: NOT a data race. CCacheEvictor::evict and CCacheReader::read both hold CSafeCache::m_mutex. The entry was evicted first and read() assumes it still exists: an ordering/logic problem. A correct answer must report that both accesses are protected by the same lock.

scenarios.title: Container cleared by another thread; tasks run on a thread pool (spawn hidden behind std::function)
scenarios.expected_conclusion: CCacheTasks::invalidate clears m_payload on one pool worker while CCacheTasks::consume on another worker calls m_payload.at(0), which throws out_of_range. Both tasks were submitted as lambdas to CThreadPool::submit; no lock protects m_payload. The pool runs tasks through an indirect std::function call.

scenarios.title: Regression: classic single-thread parameter bug (value flows through callers)
scenarios.expected_conclusion: CMenuController::selectService returns an empty string for index 3; the value flows openMenu -> CRequestBuilder::build -> CServiceValidator::validate. NOT a concurrency problem: the system must not invent a race here.
